Key Activities: As part of the area management team, contributes to the development of operational plans for census data collection activities and organizes, oversees and controls census field collection activities within the assigned geographic area; and manages census field operations for a 7-day collection operation.

Manages the financial, human and material resources for the assigned geographic area; manages employees hired under the Public Service Employment Act (PSEA); and works with recruitment teams to ensure Statistics Act employees required to meet the demands of a large temporary workforce are met for their respective areas

Develops collection strategies and contingency plans; establishes and defines priorities; monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of data collection systems and processes in their assigned geographic area; analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the activities in their assigned geographic area; and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Represents the agency in consultations with the general public to solicit participation from non-respondents, responds to and resolves complaints; and contributes to public relations activities to promote census communications and respondent cooperation.

Represents their assigned geographic area in regional and/or agency committees involved in the evaluation of census collection activities and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.
Disseminates and collects evaluation reports for the assigned geographic area; summarizes findings; and makes recommendations for program improvements.

Provides support to regional administration with the opening of the administrative hub in their geographic area such as visits during fit-up, ensures space readiness for the beginning of field activities as well as closing down activities at the hub once operations have been completed.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on: the determination and definition of objectives, content and approaches for census collection activities in the assigned geographic area and the operational framework and conditions within which the statistical program will occur; development and implementation of collection applications, alternate work methods and models to achieve desired outcomes; the development of strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes; the resolution of complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents; the development and distribution of guidelines, instructions and procedures for use by staff in their assigned geographic area; approval of appointments of all Statistics Act staff in the assigned geographic region; the assurance that financial expenditures and resources are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources in their assigned geographic area.

Decisions/recommendations taken affect the efficient and effective operations of the assigned geographic area, as well as the area’s compliance to the Statistics Act and agency policies and procedures.
Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the assigned geographic area. Establishes, coordinates and leads multidisciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, and administrative and field staff engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides training and guidance. Supervision and guidance of human resources is significant and made complex by the size and scope of a temporary workforce, and the nature of a 7-day collection operation.

Monitors expenditures for staffing and material resources to ensure funds are spent appropriately and the budget in the assigned geographic area is respected. Exercises influence and decision making latitude in allocating funds and approving expenditures in line with the financial delegation bestowed.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the assigned geographic area in accordance with agency policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.

Oversees some of the aspects related to fit-ups in the assigned geographic area with local contractors to ensure readiness at time of opening and coordinate the dismantlement of the facility at the end of census collection operation.
Communication: Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from managers, employees to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes, and briefings on program results in the assigned geographic area.
Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from the general public on the requirements for response, purpose of the census or issues with employees.

Communications skills are also required to intervene and deal with uncooperative and sometimes hostile respondents. There is a requirement to 'take control' over these emotionally-charged situations, and persuade the respondent to take a more rational approach to a situation. Strategic communication skills are required when negotiating problems of non-response or addressing problems and complaints raised by external bodies.

Negotiation skills are required to convince stakeholders when resolving problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes. Judgment, tact and flexibility are exercised in finding solutions that meet a range of business needs.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socioeconomic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to manage field operations in the assigned geographic area, analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.

In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities in the assigned geographic area and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g., confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classifications systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of census activities.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work, as well as organize, plan, schedule and control the operational activities in the assigned geographic area.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to manage staff in the delivery of the program within an assigned geographic area and ensure that work undertaken is standardized and consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the regional and local operation’s mandate, activities, priorities, standards and procedures to incorporate them into the management of the assigned geographic area and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g., confidentiality of data, security, and respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of census activities.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act, Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act, collective agreements and related policies and directives and supporting financial and human resources management methods, techniques and practices in order to manage the financial, human resource and material resources of assigned geographic areas.
Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees.

Knowledge of external business lines including those of Shared Services Canada and municipal entities are required when negotiating space requirements to facilitate the delivery of collection operations.
Research and analysis: Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes and proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.
Identifies and evaluates variations in survey responses and contributes to promotional activities to increase respondent participation rates.

Analyzes and produces reports on the progress of activities in the assigned geographic area and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Conducts comprehensive evaluations to determine the effectiveness and efficiency of collection operations. Identifies trends, gaps and inconsistencies, and makes recommendations for consideration by Head Office on areas requiring improvements or approaches to be adopted.
